report:
Fresh review of review_visibility's complete claim, two ordinary implementation entries and two ordinary tests. Captured the meta test fixture helpers and correspondence registration/span handling needed by the review capture path. No TODO/N/A evidence. Source review only: no source edits, build or tests executed.

Review capture: correspondence records the annotated module-level test as a source-spanned RustSite, retaining the function rather than substituting macro expansion. review.rs extracts that site's source range into a semantic Test fragment keyed by file/crate/target/Rust path. Thus fixture strings, annotations, explicit configuration and Expect expressions written in the function remain verbatim review input. It does not follow inline compile_test invocations into the harness implementation as part of the test fragment. Harness implementation associations are separately captured for harness claims, including this claim's compile/mod.rs run entry. Current macro forwarding retains user expressions, and run prepares outputs before invoking caller expectations, so the reviewable invocation remains the author-written test rather than generated glue.

Freshness and author intent: review.rs re-resolves each semantic Test selector and compares saved inputs against current function source. ERROR/WARN spelling and compiler conditions are source assertions, so changing them invalidates the saved review even if the expectation literal stays the same. This tooling establishes review visibility/freshness; it does not mechanically infer semantic justification. The claim's requirement that reviewers evaluate whether scenario/assertions establish behavior remains a reviewer responsibility under the captured review prompt and checklist, not something a successful blessing run can prove.

Test evidence: inline_test_capture_preserves_intent_and_excludes_macro_implementation builds a disposable meta fixture with a standalone macro definition and an associated inline test containing source, ERROR if SAGE, WARN if rustc, edition and an explicit diagnostic expectation. It asserts exact equality between the captured Test fragment and the whole inline function, asserts no captured fragment contains the macro definition, records a review and verifies validity. Changing only that unrelated macro definition keeps the semantic test capture current. It then independently changes each severity/condition spelling and requires the check to become invalid. The fixture helpers create the specification, associated implementation and normal Cargo test target, and invoke real review start/record/check, so this is substantive capture/freshness evidence rather than a string-only mock. Excluding the macro definition here does not exempt harness implementation changes from their own associated reviews.

The second test, blessing_edits_the_inline_callsite_and_then_passes_without_updates, keeps the full disposable caller fixture and its expectations visibly inside the annotated function. Its subprocess assertions prove an unexpected rustc diagnostic cannot update snapshots, stale expectations fail without writes, successful blessing edits the literal at that caller, preserves the source marker and diagnostics field, and a separate non-updating run succeeds without changes. It demonstrates why blessing is representation updating rather than authorization to change diagnostic intent. Together these tests cover whole-invocation visibility, separate harness implementation review, source-sensitive marker/condition invalidation and preserved inline assertion text. No concrete defect or requested edit found.
